name: United Way of Cullman County
summary: United Way raises money in Cullman and Winston counties and passes it to local programs for health, kids and money troubles. Volunteers help decide where the money goes. It also runs the free Imagination Library book program for young children.

name: The Link of Cullman County
summary: A family resource center that connects neighbors with local help, people and opportunities so families can get on steady ground.

name: Cullman Caring for Kids
summary: Works to stop child abuse in the county through public education and several programs. It also runs one of the county's busiest food pantries.
address: 402 Arnold Street NE Suite W-1, Cullman, AL 35055

name: Curt's Closet
summary: Kids and teens 19 and under can pick out free clothes, shoes, socks, underwear and a backpack in a shop set up like a boutique. It also helps families after a fire or other crisis.

name: Brooks' Place Child Advocacy Center
summary: A safe, child friendly place where children who may have been abused can talk with trained staff, so they face fewer interviews. If you think a child is being abused, call Cullman County DHR at (256) 737-5300 first.

name: Youth Advocate Programs, Cullman County
summary: Part of a national nonprofit that works with young people and families at home and in the community, as an option to placement away from home.

name: Cullman City Schools Foundation
summary: Raises money for Cullman City Schools, including classroom grants for teachers, and honors distinguished alumni.

name: Wallace State Future Foundation
summary: The nonprofit arm of Wallace State Community College. Gifts fund student scholarships and college programs.

name: The Willow Path
summary: Help for people facing domestic violence or sexual assault, including emergency shelter, counseling and legal advocacy. The 24 hour hotline is (256) 734-6100.

name: Crisis Services of North Alabama
summary: Serves Cullman and Winston counties with crisis counseling, advocacy and forensic nurse exams after a sexual assault. Its HELPline is free and open 24 hours.

name: Restoring Women Outreach
summary: A yearlong, 12 step based sober living program for women recovering from addiction.

name: Hope Inspired Ministries
summary: A job training program that helps people out of work get ready for a job, land one and keep it.

name: The First Source for Women
summary: A Hanceville pregnancy center offering free pregnancy tests, ultrasounds and support by appointment.

name: Lotus Health
summary: A Cullman nonprofit started in 2021 that offers health and wellness programs and events.

name: Cullman Regional Foundation
summary: The charitable arm of Cullman Regional, raising money to support care at the hospital.

name: Hope Horses
summary: Therapeutic riding for children and adults with physical, social, learning or emotional needs. Volunteers are always welcome.

name: Cullman County Center for the Developmentally Disabled
summary: Services for adults 22 and older with developmental disabilities, plus early intervention for children from birth to age 3.

name: Paws Up Rescue
summary: A foster based dog rescue in Cullman that takes in abused and neglected dogs and finds them homes.

name: Cullman County Historical Society
summary: Works to save and share Cullman County history, with a map of historic sites and murals you can tour.

name: Les Dames of Cullman
summary: A group that connects women of all ages for mentoring and community events.

name: Good Samaritan Health Clinic
summary: A health clinic for people in Cullman County who have no health insurance.
address: 401 Arnold Street NE, Suite A, Cullman, AL 35055
